interventions.speaker: EXPERT-EAU
interventions.who: EAU guideline specialist; speaks only from the guideline text he retrieved
interventions.body:
Hello, I am EXPERT-EAU. I will now search the guidelines regarding management after a prostate cancer biopsy.

**GUIDELINE**
"e patients with suspected organ-confined disease. Strong Perform limited biopsy only, without MRI, in males with clear evidence of locally advanced disease on digital rectal examination or those not for curative treatment. Weak Combine targeted biopsy with perilesional sampling when MRI is positive (i.e. PI-RADS ≥ 4)."

**WHAT THE EXPERTS DO NOT SETTLE**
The experts have not settled on a definitive management strategy post-biopsy. The decision hinges on balancing the risk of cancer versus the risk of over-treatment, particularly given the uncertainty surrounding the benefit node's AUC being at chance level.

**WHAT THE DOCUMENTS MUST SETTLE**
The documents must settle on the specific management pathway following the biopsy, particularly concerning the role of MRI in guiding subsequent steps, and the appropriate follow-up protocol (e.g., PSA monitoring frequency).

7.3.3.a
Prostate-specific antigen monitoring
Measurement of PSA is the cornerstone of follow-up after local treatment. While PSA thresholds depend on the
local treatment used, PSA recurrence almost always precedes clinical recurrence [1436, 1437]. The key question
is to establish when a PSA rise is clinically significant since not all PSA increases have the same clinical value
(see Section 6.4.2) [994]. No prospective studies are available on the optimal timing for PSA testing and the
impact on oncological outcomes.
7.3.3.a.1
Prostate-specific antigen monitoring after radical prostatectomy
Following RP, the PSA level is expected to be undetectable.

Findings: PSA measurements were 7.5 ng/mL in Nov 2022, 1.6 ng/mL in Aug 2023, 1.3 ng/mL in May 2024, and 8.8 ng/mL in Feb 2025. The trajectory shows a decline followed by a sharp increase.
**laboratory_results**
Findings: PSA is 8.8 ng/mL as of 30 Jan 2025. Free PSA is 1.12 ng/mL (13%). Other labs, including eGFR, are within normal limits.

The specific management decision following the biopsy is not recorded.
WHAT THIS SUPPORTS
The findings support the need to weigh the risk of cancer against over-treatment, as the benefit node's AUC is at chance level. The PI-RADS 4 finding and the Gleason 3+4 diagnosis are key inputs for the management discussion, especially in light of the EAU guideline suggesting limited biopsy without MRI if there is clear evidence of locally advanced disease on DRE or if not for curative treatment.

Biopsy Specimen - 12 October 2024
Histological examination of the submitted prostate tissue cores reveals adenocarcinoma with a Gleason score of 3+4, corresponding to ISUP grade group 2. The malignant glands exhibit an acinar growth pattern. No cribriform or intraductal patterns identified. Perineural invasion is absent. The tumour location is noted within the peripheral zone / transition zone, apex left.

previous_notes.author: Dr. N. Kuiper (GP)
previous_notes.text: Routine follow-up visit for blood pressure management and prostate monitoring. The patient reports feeling well with no new urinary complaints. Laboratory results from early August showed a prostate-specific antigen level of 1.6 ng/mL, representing a continued decline from previous measurements. Blood pressure remains adequately controlled on current antihypertensive therapy, and routine blood work was unremarkable.

previous_notes.author: Dr. N. Kuiper (GP)
previous_notes.text: The patient presented for scheduled urological follow-up following his recent prostate biopsy. Histological results confirmed the presence of low-grade adenocarcinoma, which was discussed in detail during the consultation. A repeat prostate-specific antigen measurement in May returned at 1.3 ng/mL, consistent with the initial post-biopsy trajectory. Given the recent sharp rise in antigen levels, the patient has been referred to the urology outpatient clinic for comprehensive re-evaluation and multidisciplinary discussion.
